_doc: Topic bank of The If Engine: vetted 'what if you' scenarios with proven pull, for days when the trend file has no strong fresh everyday scenario. Built 2026-11-15 from 1,190 short videos (28 searches: the most viewed 'what if / what happens if / why can't you / can you survive' shorts of the last 30 days and of the last year), ranked by how far a video beat the size of its channel. 'evidence' is that data. 'leads' are starting points for the facts and MUST be verified and computed (PRODUCER.md section 2), never read out as they stand. Tier A: several channels or a small channel far above its size, safe, drawable, one checkable number. Tier B: good but weaker evidence, harder to draw, or lighter on physics. An entry is used up when toon/episodes.json has an episode on it.
what_wins: A place everybody has sat in (plane seat, elevator, car, kitchen, pool) beats a place nobody has been (Jupiter, a black hole): our plane-door short got 2,589 views in its first 6 hours, our space shorts 1 to 243 views in 5 days.
The viewer has asked himself this question before: can the door open, what if the cable snaps, can I stand on a cloud, does gum stay for seven years.
A plain title a ten-year-old understands, with concrete nouns (door, elevator, cloud, gum); no technical words (metabolism, relativity).
'for 5 seconds' is a proven frame for small channels (friction: 2.7M views on a 1,640-subscriber channel; time stopped: 14.5M on 42.7k).
Airplanes are the deepest well: 60 videos, 171M views, 43 channels in the sample, 42 of them by channels under 100k subscribers.
Space works for small channels only as personal survival (an astronaut stuck floating: 54M views on a 58k channel), never as astronomy.
never: falling out of a plane, falling overboard, train tracks, house fires, crashes with victims: deaths and accidents
swallowing objects (coins, fish, magnets), microwaving things, liquid nitrogen, jumping from heights: a child could copy it
what happens inside your body when you eat, drink or take something; diets; how long without sleep, food or an organ: medical advice
weapons, crime, real people, countries and politics, games, films and superheroes

topics.question: What If the Elevator Cable Snapped?
topics.evidence: 44 elevator shorts, 60M views, 43 channels; 'cable snaps' videos reach 27k to 178k views on channels with 50 to 1,250 subscribers (up to 555 views per subscriber) in the last two weeks.
topics.leads: Elevators hang on several steel ropes, each able to hold the loaded car alone; a speed governor trips wedge brakes that grip the guide rails (Otis's 1854 demonstration); a buffer sits in the pit. Jumping at the last instant takes only a few mph off.
topics.places: new: elevator car (a box, like the cabin); the kit shaft as the elevator shaft

topics.question: What If You Jumped on a Cloud?
topics.evidence: 'what would happen if you jumped on top of a cloud' 927k views on a 6.3k-subscriber channel (147 views per subscriber); a 'fell through a cloud' copy appeared this week.
topics.leads: A small fair-weather cumulus holds about half a gram of water per cubic metre: hundreds of tonnes in all, spread so thin that it is fog. You fall straight through and come out damp.

topics.question: What If Friction Disappeared for 5 Seconds?
topics.evidence: 2.7M views on a 1,640-subscriber channel (1,653 views per subscriber, the biggest outlier of the sample).
topics.leads: Walking, braking, holding anything, knots, screws and woven cloth all rely on friction; a car at 70 mph covers about 500 feet in 5 s with no way to slow down or steer.

topics.question: What If Gravity Switched Off for 5 Seconds?
topics.evidence: the 'for 5 seconds' family: 13 videos, 46M views, 31M of them on channels under 100k subscribers.
topics.leads: Whatever moves keeps moving in a straight line: a small hop carries you tens of feet up in 5 s; the ground curves away under you (about 0.4 m at the equator); then everything comes back down at once.

topics.question: What If Time Stopped for Everyone but You?
topics.evidence: 'What If Time Stopped For 5 Seconds' 14.5M views on a 42.7k-subscriber channel; 'What If You Could Stop Time' 9.6M.
topics.leads: Frozen air would not move out of your way or into your lungs, no light would reach your eyes, no sound would travel: the superpower is a trap.

topics.question: What If Lightning Hit Your Plane?
topics.evidence: 129k views on a 686-subscriber channel; the plane cluster as a whole (60 videos, 171M views, 43 channels).
topics.leads: An airliner is struck about once a year; the current stays in the metal skin and leaves at another tip, the cabin is a Faraday cage; passengers get a flash and a bang.

topics.question: What If Both Engines Quit at 38,000 Feet?
topics.evidence: 'What Happens If a Plane's Engines Stop Mid-Flight?' 125k views on a 686-subscriber channel.
topics.leads: An airliner glides about 15 to 17 miles for each mile of height: roughly 100 miles and 20 minutes from cruise. It does not drop.

topics.question: What If You Jumped Inside a Plane Going 550 mph?
topics.evidence: relative-motion questions are evergreen ('...on a moving train' 53M views on a giant channel; we take the idea without the gun); plane cluster.
topics.leads: You already move at 550 mph with the plane and its air; a one-second jump lands on the same spot. The same reason nobody feels the ground turning at about 1,000 mph.

topics.question: What If You Skipped the Seat Belt in Turbulence?
topics.evidence: 'What Happens to Your Body in a Falling Plane' 412k views on a 12k-subscriber channel; plane cluster. Tell it as cartoon trouble with a good ending, never as an accident.
topics.leads: In severe turbulence the plane can be pushed down faster than free fall; whatever is not strapped in 'falls up' to the ceiling, about a metre in half a second.

topics.question: What If the Landing Gear Didn't Come Down?
topics.evidence: 852k views on a 2.3k-subscriber channel (374 views per subscriber); its sequel on runway overruns 347k.
topics.leads: A belly landing: metal sliding on the runway brakes hard, sparks fly, airliners and crews are prepared for it and people walk away.
topics.places: cabin and sky (plane-door-midflight); the runway strip of that episode's last shot

topics.question: What If You Stuck Your Hand Out of a Plane Window?
topics.evidence: 231k views on a 2.6k-subscriber channel.
topics.leads: At 550 mph in the thin air of 38,000 ft the wind presses with about 1.5 psi: 30 to 40 lb on an open hand, in air near minus 70 F. And the window cannot open, for the door's reason.

topics.question: Could You Fly Through Space by Farting?
topics.evidence: 'What if You Fart in Space' 57M and 'Fart In A Space Suit' 25M (giant channels); 'If You Fart in a Silent Elevator' 3.4M on an 18.7k-subscriber channel this week.
topics.leads: A tenth of a gram of gas at a few metres per second moves a suited astronaut by a few millionths of a metre per second: 1 mph would take more than a hundred thousand of them.
topics.places: earth (kit, space light); Gus already wears the helmet

topics.question: What If You Took Off Your Helmet in Space?
topics.evidence: 'What Happens If An Astronaut Gets Stuck Floating In Space?' 54M views on a 58k-subscriber channel (927 views per subscriber); 'How Long You'd Survive On The Moon' 17.9M on 223k.
topics.leads: No explosion and no instant freezing: about 10 to 15 seconds of consciousness, the moisture on the tongue boils (reported after a 1960s vacuum-chamber accident), fine again if the helmet goes back on in time. Gus puts it back on.

topics.question: What If You Lived on a Planet the Size of a House?
topics.evidence: 2.7M views on a 42.7k-subscriber channel.
topics.leads: A rock ball 10 m across has less than a millionth of Earth's gravity: you weigh as much as a grain of rice, one step throws you off for good (escape speed of millimetres per second), the horizon is two steps away.
topics.places: new: a small sphere in the kit's space light

topics.question: What If You Could Live on Sunlight Like a Plant?
topics.evidence: 'What If Humans Could Photosynthesize' 821k views on a 42.7k-subscriber channel, plus two copies in other languages.
topics.leads: Under two square metres of skin, sunlight of about 1,000 W per square metre, plants keep 1 to 2 % of it: a whole day in the sun buys a cookie or two against the 2,000 calories a body burns.

topics.question: What If an Immortal Snail Was Chasing You?
topics.evidence: 'Why You Can't Escape The Immortal Snail' 6.7M views on a 5.5k-subscriber channel (1,216 views per subscriber); two more snail rows with 4.8M and 0.3M.
topics.leads: A garden snail covers metres per hour: you out-walk a day of its travel in minutes, and a trip around the world takes it centuries. Compute how much head start each night's sleep costs.

topics.question: What If You Swallowed Your Gum?
topics.evidence: 27 gum and watermelon-seed shorts, 28M views, 26 channels; the seed one has 9.9M on a 32k-subscriber channel. Food myths only: never objects.
topics.leads: Gum base is not digested, but it travels with everything else and is gone in a few days; the seven years are a myth. A swallowed seed does not sprout either.
topics.places: garden; the inside of the body as flat diagram cards

topics.question: How Many Balloons Would It Take to Lift You?
topics.evidence: a classic that is not in this month's sample; safe and very visual.
topics.leads: One party balloon lifts about 14 grams: several thousand for an adult.

topics.question: What If You Dropped a Penny From a Skyscraper?
topics.evidence: 'dropped 10kg of tungsten from space' 9.4M and 8.7M views on a 63.5k-subscriber channel. Show that it flutters harmlessly; do not make dropping things look like a game.
topics.leads: A penny tumbles and stops speeding up at 30 to 50 mph: a sting at most.

topics.question: What If You Could Run 100 mph?
topics.evidence: 'What If You Could Run 10x Faster?' 990k views on a 37.5k-subscriber channel.
topics.leads: Air drag, the force on each foot strike and the power needed all rise steeply with speed: compute the horsepower.

topics.question: What If Every Mosquito Vanished?
topics.evidence: 3.1M views on a 6.9k-subscriber channel and 4.1M on a 42.7k one. Ecology, so cite numbers rather than compute them.
topics.leads: Thousands of species, a few bite people; what eats them and what they pollinate.

topics.question: What If You Left a Soda Can in a Hot Car?
topics.evidence: '...Plastic Bottles In Your Car' 1.9M in 2 days (giant channel); 'Truck Tire Blows Out at 60 MPH' 5.9M on a 40.9k one.
topics.leads: A closed car in the sun passes 140 F inside; the pressure in a can climbs with temperature until the lid gives.
topics.places: new: a car on the kit's street

topics.question: What If Your Ice Cream Was as Cold as Space?
topics.evidence: 'What if your Ice-cream got Colder every 2 Seconds?' 6.0M views on a 63.5k-subscriber channel; 'What If You Hit Absolute Zero?' 17.7M (giant).
topics.leads: How fast heat leaves, why it would stick to the tongue, how hard it gets.

topics.question: What If Everyone on Earth Jumped at Once?
topics.evidence: 'What if everyone...' has 36 videos and 38M views, but mostly through giant channels.
topics.leads: The planet moves by less than the width of an atom and moves back; the real problem is elsewhere.

topics.question: What If You Shrank to the Size of an Ant?
topics.evidence: the reverse, 'What If You Grew Four Times Bigger', has 16M views (giant channel); not in the small-channel data.
topics.leads: Strength per weight goes up, falls stop hurting, but heat leaks out and a water drop becomes a trap. (Different angle from the hummingbird episode: no food, no heat balance.)

topics.question: What If You Were Born on the Moon?
topics.evidence: 26M views (giant channel); 'This Is How Long You'd Survive On The Moon' 17.9M on a 223k one.
topics.leads: One sixth of the weight for a growing body, and the trip to Earth afterwards.
topics.places: new: a moon surface (kit space light)

topics.question: What If You Left the Fridge Open to Cool Your Kitchen?
topics.evidence: no rows in the sample; an everyday myth with a surprising answer.
topics.leads: A fridge moves heat from its inside to its back: with the door open the room gets warmer, by the power it draws.

topics.question: Could You Heat Your Coffee by Yelling at It?
topics.evidence: no rows in the sample; a funny number.
topics.leads: A shout carries about a thousandth of a watt of sound: compute the months of yelling one cup needs.

topics.question: What If You Dropped Your Phone From a Plane?
topics.evidence: phone-survival tests draw millions ('How many folds can the iPhone Duo survive??' 6.0M); plane cluster.
topics.leads: A phone tumbles and stops speeding up well under 100 mph, so the height hardly matters; what it lands on does.

topics.question: What If the Sun Switched Off for 5 Seconds?
topics.evidence: 'What if Our Sun Disappeared' 55M views (giant channel) joined with the 'for 5 seconds' frame.
topics.leads: Nobody would notice for 8 minutes 20 seconds, and then for exactly 5 seconds.

topics.question: What If You Could Never Die?
topics.evidence: 9 videos, 19M views; 471k on an 8k-subscriber channel. Light on physics: needs a numbers angle (what the far future does to an immortal).
topics.leads: Time scales of the Sun, of the Earth, of the stars.
